# Eventloupe

> Eventloupe is a Chrome DevTools extension, "a magnifier for tracking events". It shows every pixel, tag and dataLayer push a page fires, what was sent, and what was actually observed. Each event is marked observed, failed or unknown, and traced through six stages from the page to the server's response.

Status: launching soon on the Chrome Web Store.

## Key facts
- Covers 21 sources in one DevTools panel: dataLayer, Google Analytics 4, Google Tag Manager, Meta Pixel, TikTok, Google Ads, Snapchat, Pinterest, LinkedIn, Reddit, Segment, Adobe Analytics, Amplitude, Mixpanel, Microsoft UET, X, Criteo, Floodlight/CM360, Taboola, Outbrain and Quora.
- Three evidence states, never two: observed (for example HTTP 204), failed (for example HTTP 500) and unknown (not observable, recorded as null instead of guessed).
- Six pipeline stages: Application, Tag Manager, SDK invocation, Network, Response, Correlation.
- Diagnostics are rule-based with permanent codes from EL1000 to EL9999. The same input always gives the same result, and a code never fires on missing evidence alone.
- The extension observes requests and never blocks or modifies them.
- The extension collects, transmits and stores no data outside the browser. It has no accounts, servers or analytics.

## Pages
- [Home](https://eventloupe.com/): overview, comparison with pass/fail debuggers, diagnostic code examples and FAQ.
- [Docs](https://eventloupe.com/docs.html): opening the panel, reading an event, the six stages, code ranges, permissions and FAQ.
- [Privacy policy](https://eventloupe.com/privacy.html): what the extension reads, how data is stored, permissions, and how this website's optional analytics work.
- [Full documentation text for LLMs](https://eventloupe.com/llms-full.txt): the docs page as plain text.
